text.p: Programme of matches in French first division this week (kickoff times GMT):
On Thursday:
Rennes v Lyon 1630

Lyon have midfielder Stephane Roche in squad after missing 1-0 home defeat by Metz because of sunstroke. Rennes, hoping to maintain last season's good form at home, could give debut to German striker Patrick Weiser.
Auxerre v Paris St Germain 1830

Last season's European Cup quarter-finalists Auxerre will be looking to escape quickly from foot of table after 3-0 defeat at Lens with France international goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier back from injury. PSG should be unchanged from 2-0 home win over promoted Chateauroux with Brazilians Leonardo on international duty and newly signed Edmilson not match fit.
On Friday: all 1800
Bastia v Guingamp

Guingamp made three-goal start against Cannes, arguably weakest team in division, but should find Corsicans harder to handle away. Bastia, who won 1-0 at Nantes, welcome back Liberian forward Prince Daye after suspension.
Monaco v Chateauroux

Champions have defender Martin Djetou and midfielder Sylvain Legwinski back from injury after opening title defence with 1-0 loss at Bordeaux. They should beat promoted side unlucky to meet big guns in first two games after 2-0 defeat away to PSG.
Cannes v Toulouse
Goalkeeper Gregory Wimbee is doubtful for Cannes, whose coach Addick Koot believes second division runners-up Toulouse could spring several surprises in top flight this season.
Metz v Bordeaux

Clash of two championship outsiders who both won 1-0 on opening day. Bordeaux should retain side that beat champions Monaco with newly signed Dutchman Kiki Musampa and Sylvain Wiltord not match fit, though they will be on bench, while defender Romain Ferrier is still out with injury.
Marseille v Nantes

Midfielder Teddy Bertin is out of Marseille side with sciatica, but midfielder Frederic Brando is available after suspension. Nantes defender Erix Decroix is back from injury, but strikers Javier Mazzoni and Samba N'Diaye are doubtful as they look to bounce back from home defeat by Bastia.
Le Havre v Montpellier

Former PSG and France striker Cyril Pouget, fellow forward Lionel Prat and Greek defender Marinos Ouzunidis are fit to stregthen Le Havre side beaten 3-1 at Marseille. Montpellier look to talented Ivorian Ibrahim Bakayoko, scorer in 1-1 draw with Strasbourg, for goals.
Strasbourg v Lens Lens look good enough to repeat fine start last season when
they won first four games and improve on that. Strasbourg hope impressive strike pair David Zitelli and Pascal Nouma come good.
